question.leadin: In 1845, a British flagstaff was controversially cut down in this modern country, sparking a year of war.
question.text: Name this Oceanic nation consisting of a North Island, South Island, and many small islands roughly one thousand miles east of Australia.
question.clue: In 1893 it became the first country to have universal women's suffrage, and it earlier saw a gold rush centered on Dunedin ("doo-nay-din").

swap.leadin: If you're going on a vacation to the Aloha State, you might fly into this city's Daniel K. Inouye (IN-ooh-wee) International Airport.
swap.text: Name this capital city of Hawaii. It is home to the only royal palace in the USA, Iolani Palace, as well as Waikiki Beach.
swap.clue: Tourists often laugh when they discover that even Hawaii has "interstate highways," something that manylearn upon landing at Daniel Inouye[ee-noh-ay]InternationalAirport in this city.

question.text: This document disenfranchised many non-whites and allowed Americans to vote in Hawaii without being citizens. This document was named for the way that Lorrin Thurston forced it upon King Kalakaua.
question.clue: It was designed to break the power of Premier Walter Gibson and spawned a failed counterrevolution led by Robert Wilcox.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about the Spanish-American War.
swap.text: As a result of the war, the U.S. gained control of this island, the largest of the Marianas ("mare-ee-AHN-us"). It is still an American territory today.
swap.clue: The 1950 Organic Act of this territory granted its residents citizenship, and a 1968 amendment of that act allowed this territory to elect a governor.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Polynesian kingdoms.
question.text: This kingdom was founded by Pomare I and controlled much of the Society Islands and surrounding archipelagos. This kingdom was eventually conquered by the French, and is still under French control today.
question.clue: This Kingdom, which achieved short-lived protectorate status via the 1847 Jarnac Convention. Its final King, Pomare V, was forced to abdicate in 1880.

swap.text: Taking place between June 4 and June 7, 1942, a month after Coral Sea, four Japanese aircraft carriers sunk at this battle on an atoll northwest of Hawaii. America lost one aircraft carrier and one destroyer.
swap.clue: William Halsey was sidelined from a battle at this location due to an outbreak of eczema and had to be replaced by Raymond Spruance.

question.text: Thanks to a quarantine imposed by John Martin Poyer, this Pacific territory of the United States avoided the Spanish flu pandemic. This southernmost territory of the US has its capital at Pago Pago.
question.answerHtml: American Samoa [or Amerika Samoa; prompt on Samoan Islands but reject “Samoa”]
question.clue: This territory has the highest rate of military service of any in the United States.

swap.leadin: This event ended at Camp O'Donnell.
swap.text: Name this event, in which Japanese troops led by Masaharu Homma forcibly marched prisoners of war across the island of Luzon. Homma was later executed for his role in this event.
swap.clue: During World War II, tens of thousands of Filipino and American P.O.W.s were sent on a death march named for this Philippine peninsula. Over ten thousand Filipino P.O.W.s were killed on this death march.

question.leadin: Answer the following about items in the collection of Berlin's controversial Humboldt Forum.
question.text: The Forum owns a feather cloak once worn by this monarch that was gifted to Frederick William III of Prussia. This king conquered the Hawaiian islands in the 1780s.
question.answerHtml: King Kamehameha I [or Kamehameha the Great; or Paiea; prompt on Kamehameha]
question.clue: After being attacked by fishermen during a war, this king promoted the safety of civilians in the Law of the Splintered Paddle.

swap.text: This monarch of another short-lived country was deposed outside the ʻIolani Palace by American-backed revolutionaries. This monarch opposed a king's signing of the Bayonet Constitution.
swap.clue: John L. Stevens was found to support anti-royalist conspirators in a report finding that the overthrow of this ruler was illegal, named for James H. Blount.

question.text: The Allied capture of Guadalcanal allowed the Allied troops to begin this strategy of capturing less-fortified locations in order to deprive stronger but more distant locations of resources.
question.clue: This strategy eventually adopted by the United States in the Pacific Theater of World War II, which ignored heavily fortified Japanese strongholds and focused on capturing less-defended areas that could be used as bases.

swap.leadin: A 2000 coup in this country resulted in the overthrow of its ethnically Indian prime minister Mahendra Choudhry.
swap.text: Name this Pacific island country, where Indian indentured laborers were brought to work on plantations. Prior to becoming a British colony, this country was united into a short-lived kingdom by the warlord Cakobau.
swap.clue: Sitiveni Rabuka declared this country a republic after taking power in 1987.

question.text: Modern cases for reparations for 19th century land confiscations are heard by a tribunal named for this North Island town. William Hobson's signing of a document named for this town is a National Holiday in New Zealand.

swap.leadin: Three layers of coral rock slabs surrounded ancient hills called langi that served as the burial sites of royals from an empire in this modern-day country.
swap.text: Name this modern-day country, the center of an empire known as "Tu'i [this country]." This country has its capital at Nuku'alofa.
swap.clue: This country lost much of its invested capital when former Bank of America financial advisor and honorary court jester Jesse Bogdonoff lost almost all of the profit it had made selling passports to foreigners.

question.text: Marquesan legend tells of how traders from this kingdom exchanged red kula feathers throughout Polynesia, including with James Cook, who called its islands "Friendly" for his warm reception by its monarch, the Tu'i.
question.answerHtml: Tonga [or Kingdom of Tonga or Pule‘anga Fakatu‘i ‘o Tonga; accept Tu’i Tonga Empire or Tongan Empire]
question.clue: Many examples of dance-poems called lakalaka were composed by this country's 20th century queen Salote.

swap.leadin: Members of this ethnic group got into altercations with Chilean police that led to shooting in December 2010.
swap.text: Identify this ethnic group that is has been occupying buildings to demand the return of their ancestor's homes that were seized by the government.
swap.clue: This place is where the undeciphered rongorongo script developed.

question.text: Bougainville also tried to name parts of this Pacific island nation after himself. The American libertarian Phoenix Foundation funded the Nagriamel Movement's secession attempts after its independence under Walter Lini.
question.clue: This nation's colonial system was dubbed the Pandemonium, because it was a really wasteful condominium system shared by Britain and France.

swap.leadin: This island was the primary base of the Arioi ("ar-ee-OI"), a secret society whose members traveled between islands to carry out Dionysian rituals and maintain traditional culture.
swap.text: Name this island that was ruled for much of the 18th and 19th centuries by the Pomare dynasty. The Royal Society sponsored a mission to this island to observe the 1769 transit of Venus.
swap.clue: That dynasty also saw the fifty-year reign of queen ʻAimata, during whose rule the Consul George Pritchard was expelled by admiral Dupetit Thouars.

question.text: After the Philippine Sea, Mitscher attacked this lagoon in the Caroline Islands in Operation Hailstone. This location has been called the Japanese Pearl Harbor since it thus became a graveyard for most of the Japanese ships and planes in the South Pacific.
question.clue: Operation Hailstone targeted this Japanese base in Micronesia in a surprise attack of February 1944, sinking forty ships in what has been called "Japan's Pearl Harbor."

swap.text: Congreve rockets were first used against the Maori to unsuccessfully attack a pa held by this leader. This leader began the Flagstaff War by repeatedly chopping down British flagpoles on Maiki Hill.
swap.clue: While recovering from wounds at an earlier battle, this man entrusted his ally to oppose Henry Despard at the Battle of Ohaeawai.
